title: How Buffett ran his partnership 1962-64: beat the Dow, buy cheap, compound, measure honestly
summary: Buffett's partnership letters from 1962 to mid-1964 explain his three investing categories (generals, workouts, controls), why results should be judged against the Dow over three years or more, and how a wide margin of safety drove returns. Dempster Mill shows value buying and capital reallocation in practice. He also covers compounding, taxes, and alignment with partners.

principles.text: Judge performance against a pre-chosen benchmark, not by whether the year is up or down.
principles.quote: Whether we do a good job or a poor job is not to be measured by whether we are plus or minus for the year. It is instead to be measured against the general experience in securities as measured by the Dow- Jones Industrial Average

principles.text: Short-term results are noise; give any strategy at least three years.
principles.quote: While I much prefer a five-year test, I feel three years is an absolute minimum for judging performance.

principles.text: Buy at prices so attractive that a mediocre sale still works; never count on a great exit.
principles.quote: Never count on making a good sale. Have the purchase price be so attractive that even a mediocre sale gives good results.

principles.text: True conservatism comes from correct facts and reasoning, not from popular agreement.
principles.quote: You will not be right simply because a large number of people momentarily agree with you. You will not be right simply because important people agree with you.

principles.text: Don't predict the market; pick investments on value and limit permanent capital loss with a margin of safety and diversification.
principles.quote: I am not in the business of predicting general stock market or business fluctuations. If you think I can do this, or think it is essential to an investment program, you should not be in the partnership.

principles.text: Small differences in compounding rate become enormous over long periods.
principles.quote: It is obvious that a variation of merely a few percentage points has an enormous effect on the success of a compounding (investment) program.
